text:
maria.chen: Quick q — I'm putting together a small offload contract between the runtime and quantization profiles. Goal: let runtime decide fast but give infra enough signal to route/burst/fallback with safety. Sketch below.

maria.chen: proposed header (very rough):
```json
{
  "quant_profile": "fp8-aggressive-v2",
  "quality_budget_pct": 0.6,    // allowed relative quality drop vs baseline
  "fallback_tag": "int8-safe",
  "max_extra_latency_ms": 15,
  "degradation_estimate": 0.03  // estimated delta on key eval metric
}
```

devon: I like the idea. Quick nit: "quality_budget_pct" read as percent-of-baseline or percent points? I'd prefer an absolute delta field (e.g. max_neg_logprob_delta) because percents are ambiguous across tasks.

nina: telemetry reqs: we need events for quant.switch, quant.fallback, quant.estimate with fields: request_id, profile_from, profile_to, reason, sample_prompt_id. Also include model_version and token_counts.

samir: runtime complexity warning — the more decision knobs we shove into the header, the more the runtime has to understand. Suggest minimal runtime contract: {preferred_profile, safety_policy_id, optional_hard_limits}. Leave routing/placement to a separate service that consumes telemetry.

pranay: Canary + rollback basics need to be part of the contract. Add two optional fields: canary_fraction (0-1) and grace_period_min. Example: canary_fraction=0.05, grace_period_min=30. If degradation_estimate > threshold during grace period -> auto-roll to fallback_tag.

maria.chen: Agree with keeping runtime surface small but we still need a compact, machine-readable estimate so infra can do quick HPA/burst decisions (e.g. dodge fallback pools when quality hit is expected to be large).

devon: Another compatibility thing: add profile_v (int) and a freeform notes field. Backwards compatible if runtime ignores unknown keys.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started for fp8-aggressive-v2 -> 5% traffic in us-west (canary id cny-781).

nina: Also add quality_probe_ids: [eval_set_12, smoke_qa_3] so infra can trigger targeted eval replays during canary.

samir: For safety: require fallback pools to be heterogeneous (cross-az or cross-region) if max_extra_latency_ms > X, otherwise we're exposing single-point degradation. Put that as an ops-level check, not runtime.

maria.chen: Action items: devon to draft proto for header and v1 compatibility, samir to sketch minimal runtime shim that only reads (preferred_profile, safety_policy_id, hard_limits), nina to enumerate telemetry fields and probe ids, pranay to add canary playbook with auto-rollback rules. I'll iterate on exact field names and publish a short RFC. :thumbsup:

devon: ack. I can start a proto PR today.

pranay: will draft playbook and link to incident runbook.

nina: will post telemetry schema in #eng-infra once drafted.

samir: will mock up the shim and perf overhead estimate.

maria.chen: thanks all — will follow up with a tiny RFC (1 pager).
